rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods <U+2013> two-year (2005, 2006) replicated field experiment at Talat Demiroren research station comparing subsurface and surface drip systems at six irrigation levels on muskmelon. Q2: Results and conclusions, Table 3 and Fig. 1 <U+2013> yields reported for both systems; quadratic regression with a dummy for system showed no significant difference between subsurface and surface drip over both years, but surface drip gave significantly higher yield in 2005 and subsurface drip significantly higher in 2006; conclusions state SSDI used about 10% less water and produced the same yield.
rows.notes: Supports the 'mixed/controversial' framing: the study's own result on SSDI versus surface drip yield is inconsistent between years and non-significant overall. Evidence rests on a single method (plot yield measurement) at one site with one crop; no intermediate variable such as soil water or evaporation was measured for the system comparison; no SD/CI reported (only letter groupings and regression r2); no explicit limitations stated; the recommendation of SSDI under limited freshwater is a recommendation, not a stated requirement for the yield effect.

notes: Full text appears complete. Study is a two-year plot trial in Sanliurfa, Turkey (clay soil, semi-arid), comparing subsurface and surface drip at 0<U+2013>125% of class A pan evaporation for muskmelon.
